item.title: Field Notes on Reliable Agents (5): Autonomy That Won't Nuke the Wrong Thing
item.description:
The previous four notes were about verification — proving work happened. This one is about the opposite risk: letting an agent take destructive action on its own, and having it confidently destroy the wrong thing.

Autonomy is the entire reason to build agents. An agent that has to ask permission for every action isn’t automation, it’s a slow human with extra steps. But the failure mode of autonomy is uniquely bad: a human who deletes the wrong row usually notices and stops; an agent executing a plan will happily delete the wrong row, then the next, then the next, at machine speed and with total confidence.
